newsitem.title: USA: Stocks firm at midday, techs and bonds lead.
newsitem.headline: Stocks firm at midday, techs and bonds lead.

text.p: Stocks rallied Wednesday as the bond market recovered its footing and technology issues surged after Microsoft Corp. said it would invest in Apple Computer Inc.

Just after 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 53.88 points at 8,241.42. In the broader market, gaining issues beat declines by a 17-10 margin on active volume of about 315 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
High-tech issues showed strength and again lifted the broader stock market. The Nasdaq composite index rose 8.92 points to 1,630.45, moving further into record territory.

"The bond market is recovering, which is helping stocks," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany. "Plus, Apple is very dramatic, with the board changes and the Microsoft investment. It has given a real lift to markets."

Blue chips languished earlier this week as long-term interest rates rose on renewed investor worries about inflation. But the 30-share Dow turned around as bonds erased losses ahead of Wednesday's Treasury auction of $12 billion of 10-year notes and the release of the Federal Reserve's periodic review of economic conditions.
"Today appears to be more of catch-up day for the Dow, which had been struggling lately," said Greg Nie, technical analyst at Everen Securities.
Most analysts had not expected the bond market to recover until after Thursday, when the Treasury was scheduled to sell $10 billion in 30-year bonds, Johnson said.
"The bond market rebound is coming a little earlier than expected, which is very good news," he said.
The 30-year Treasury rose an eighth of a point, lowering its yield, which moves in the opposite direction, to 6.48 percent from 6.49 percent Tuesday.
Microsoft's announcement that it would invest $150 million in Apple boosted tech stocks and the broader market, analysts said.
"The technology market was looking for an excuse to rally and the excitement around Apple gave traders that excuse," said Frank Calta, managing director of institutional trading at Dain Bosworth.
Apple's stock soared 6-1/2 to 26-1/4 in active trading. The company also set a series of alliances with Microsoft and revamped its board of directors.
Microsoft rose 3/8 to 143-11/16, International Business Machines gained 1-5/8 to 108-1/8 and Dell Computer added 1-5/8 to 83-1/4.
Elsewhere, ITT Corp. rose 2 to 64-15/16 after Hilton Hotels Corp. raised its hostile takeover bid for rival ITT Corp. to $70 a share from its previous offer of $55 a share.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks rose 5.60 to 957.97.
The American Stock Exchange index added 1.68 to 652.33.
